notes.2: Many candidates had difficulty in interpreting the graphs and worked as though the vertical axis showed the distance that each rocket had travelled.
notes.3: Some candidates did not recognise that the distance travelled by the train was measured in kilometres and the time in minutes, whereas in the responses the average speeds were given in metres per second.
notes.8: Some candidates believed that hydroelectric power involves the heating of water to produce high pressure steam. This fundamental error showed a lack of understanding of the generation of electricity.
notes.9: Almost equal numbers of candidates chose options A , B or C . Candidates appeared to be unsure of how to calculate the weight of child Y.
notes.18: Candidates did not seem to be familiar with this type of experiment. Many thought that the variable being used to measure the temperature was the length of the pointer.
notes.19: This question was challenging for many candidates and they found it difficult to understand that when a solid melts or a liquid boils, the temperature does not change until all the material has melted or vaporised.
notes.20: This question tested the knowledge that dull black surfaces are the best radiators of thermal energy. Only stronger candidates gave the correct answer, with many weaker candidates thinking that a shiny white surface was the best radiator.
notes.29: Only stronger candidates answered this correctly. The increase in the reading on the balance indicated that the upper rod pushes down on the lower rod, meaning they repel, which in turn means that either they both carry positive charge or they both carry negative charge.
notes.33: The strongest candidates were able to answer this question correctly.
notes.35: The question was answered well by stronger candidates but others found it very difficult to understand that induction of an e.m.f. occurs when a magnetic field is actually changing.
notes.general_comments: There were some strong performances this year, but also some candidates who were unable to demonstrate a good understanding of scientific principles. Questions 1 , 4 , 11 , 14 , 23 , 24 and 34 were usually answered very well but Questions 2 , 9 , 19 , 29 , 33 , 35 and 39 were more challenging for many candidates.
